Stated Claim / Post Context:
Man detained at New Jersey's Delaney Hall dies in ICE custody

 A 41-year-old man detained at a private immigration detention facility in New Jersey has died, raising concerns about Delaney Hall Detention Facility

Actual Article Body:
article ul	li { list-style: disc; padding: 5px 0; }
		
		
				
			
			
				
		
		

Aug. 3 (UPI) -- A 41-year-old man detained at a private immigration detention facility in New Jersey has died, the Trump administration said Monday, further raising concerns for the safety of migrants in Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody and specifically at Delaney Hall Detention Facility.

Edwin Lopez-Cornejo, a Salvadoran national, died Saturday at University Hospital in Newark, N.J., where he was taken after experiencing a medical emergency at Delaney Hall, which is privately operated by the GEO Group under a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement contract.

He is at least the 54th person to die in ICE custody since President Donald Trump's return to office, according to a UPI count of ICE detainee-death reports.

According to Democratic lawmakers, Lopez-Cornejo, a father of a 12-year-old daughter, had been in the country for more than 20 years. ICE said he originally entered the United States in August 2006 and was removed from the country that October. It was unclear when he re-entered the country, but ICE said he was arrested by immigration law enforcement on June 18 amid Trump's aggressive immigration crackdown.



freestar.config.enabled_slots.push({ placementName: "upi-com_incontent_reusable", slotId: "upi-com_incontent_reusable_79102" });

ICE said Lopez-Cornejo received proper medical care and was seen by medical professionals. The official cause of death remains pending further medical examination, it said.

Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said in a recorded statement that Lopez-Cornejo died of an apparent heart attack. Rep. Rob Menendez, D-N.J., said in a recorded statement of his own that Lopez-Cornejo had complained of "difficulties" he was experiencing before collapsing at the detention facility.

Detention facility staff performed CPR on Lopez-Cornejo, who was then transported by emergency services to the hospital, where he was pronounced dead Saturday afternoon, Menendez said, adding that lawmakers asked ICE medical questions about the man's medical care and death but were told they would need to make a formal request.

According to Menendez, Lopez-Cornejo died weeks after another man suffered what lawmakers believe was a seizure shortly after being detained and Delaney Hall last month and was transferred to the hospital, where he later died.

"You didn't hear about this because they released him to University Hospital, so he was no longer in ICE custody," he said.

According to an ICE document dated June 2, ICE eliminated a provision from its detainee-death reporting policy, meaning it was no longer required to make public certain deaths occurring within 30 days after a person's release from custody.

Menendez said ICE changed its policy to keep the number of detainee deaths in ICE custody as low as possible.

"So you have two deaths within a matter of weeks of each other," he said.

If confirmed, It would be at least the third death connected to Delaney Hall in the last 12 months, including Jean Wilson Brutus, a 41-year-old Haitian immigrant, who died Dec. 12, 2025, a day after arriving at the facility. ICE officially reported two deaths of people detained at Delaney Hall.

During a congressional hearing on the conditions at Delaney Hall held less than two weeks ago, Amol Sinha, executive director of the American Civil Liberties Union of New Jersey, alleged a "pattern" of neglect at the facility, saying detainees there lack access to medical care, live in unsanitary conditions, eat inedible food and live with broken air conditioning in 100-degree temperatures.
